title: Query.Farm: acquire a complete result edition and operate its retained SQL service

task.name: Acquire and use the selected complete data edition through the existing VGI service
task.purpose: Give the selected customer a useful, typed dataset or discrete computation result in its existing DuckDB/Arrow application, with explicit purchase approval and repeated SQL use of the acquired edition.
task.request: Select one real customer, one authorized source or worker and one named useful result. Retain the complete source population, parameters, edition and price before an explicit acquisition. Receive all pages or batches, bind that acquired edition in the original VGI catalog and operate the customer's actual SQL task. Keep discovery, catalog binding, scans, caching and reopening on the retained acquisition. A changed edition or separately priced function invocation requires its own explicit selection and approval.
task.completeOutput: The full selected result is usable in the customer's original VGI/DuckDB receiving application, with its typed schema, population and completeness manifest, original acquisition and payment references, retained result bytes and actual useful SQL output. Deliver the original catalog/worker configuration references, retained acquired-edition state and a complete receiving package that the named operator independently reopens.
task.repeatTrigger: A new source edition or a separately requested useful computation changes the customer's actual decision or work. The customer explicitly selects that result before a new acquisition. SQL reads, cache misses, reconnects, catalog discovery and reopening the same acquired edition continue the existing purchase.
task.pricedUnit: One explicit acquisition of the named complete result edition, or one separately selected discrete function result. Bind the merchant's original exact atomic price and spending authority to that unit; retain per-request charges separately when the actual source contract requires several requests for one complete useful task.

source.reference: The customer's authorized DuckDB, Parquet or original worker source, selected complete edition and installed VGI service. Maintained receiving entry: stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf88-operator-buyer-cli/python/stellar_forge_buyer/vgi_service/README.md.
source.population: The complete agreed table, partition range or parameterized computation result, including every original page or Arrow batch required by the selected customer task. Select two real source editions when the commissioning agreement includes refresh/change handling.
source.meaning: Retain the source's field names, integer and decimal precision, timestamps and timezone, units, null semantics, row identity, parameters and ordering when meaningful. Record result completeness and any upstream restriction. Bind SQL to the acquired edition and its retained original token/state; a displayed SQL sample or LIMIT query describes that sample only.
source.changePolicy: The source owner selects a changed edition, schema or worker release. Preserve the prior acquired result and catalog entry while reviewing compatibility, completeness, authority and price for the next edition. Catalog discovery, rebinding and normal SQL execution retain the existing purchase; only the separately approved acquisition changes it.

receiving.application: The customer's existing VGI catalog/worker and DuckDB/Arrow application, composed with the maintained Stellar Forge VGI receiving service. Select the actual installed component editions, original merchant/buyer workspace and authorized receiving host.
receiving.acceptanceRule: Receive the original source and commercial selection; acquire the complete first result through the original merchant/buyer flow; run the agreed useful SQL and retain its result; demonstrate complete paging/batching and exact schema/values; reopen the same edition with its retained acquisition; select and receive the second actual edition when contracted; reopen the complete installation independently on the named host and hand over operation and support.
receiving.changeAndWithdraw: The source owner controls source publication and withdrawal; the merchant controls pricing and acquisition authority; the VGI operator controls catalog and worker releases. Select streaming or direct-file access according to the actual access policy. Streaming can apply the agreed row/column policy; direct file access grants the selected file's contents and must match the customer's permitted boundary.
receiving.recovery: Inspect the original acquisition, transfer and retained result after interruption. Resume or reopen the same result and original catalog state using the maintained receiving path. If payment completed while delivery was interrupted, recover delivery on that original purchase. Preserve complete result bytes, edition identity, private credential references and source release history when moving the installation.
receiving.maintenance: Name the source publisher, catalog/worker release owner, merchant payment operator, customer SQL owner and receiving engineer. Retain actual hosting, source/worker licenses, access renewal, refresh cadence, monitoring, rollback and correction/support allowance from the agreement. Scope any new source, customer, worker or edition policy through the original case.

steps.title: Select the original customer and useful result
steps.result: Continue the retained Workshare and Installation. Bind one customer, the actual source/worker, complete population, useful SQL task, receiving host and explicit acquisition unit. Retain the source edition and commercial terms.

steps.title: Choose the delivery and access boundary
steps.result: Select the actual VGI catalog and installed worker/service editions. Choose streaming or direct-file access from the permitted population and access policy. Record source-use rights and component licenses with the original configuration.

steps.title: Receive a complete first edition
steps.result: Use the original merchant/buyer acquisition operation with its selected network, exact atomic amount, budget and authority. Retain every required page or batch, source identity, typed schema, population and original payment/result references.

steps.title: Operate the customer's SQL work
steps.result: Bind the retained edition in the existing catalog, run the customer's actual DuckDB/Arrow work and deliver the useful result. Keep exact integer/decimal/time/null values and record how complete source coverage was established.

steps.title: Use the acquired edition repeatedly
steps.result: Reconnect, rebind, scan, cache and reopen through the maintained service using the same acquired edition. Recover an interrupted delivery or session through its original identities and retained bytes.

steps.title: Receive a deliberate changed edition
steps.result: When contracted, acquire the second real edition after its source, price and authority are selected. Retain both editions and explain the meaningful data/result change, schema treatment and explicit renewal choice.

steps.title: Receive the whole installation
steps.result: Export the complete original installation and retained application/source state. The named engineer opens the complete receiving package on the selected host, reruns the actual useful task and confirms access, refresh, payment, release, correction and support ownership.

inputs: Original complete customer Workshare commissioning source and matching receiving packet, case identity, plan digest and existing Installation identity when already saved
Authorized actual source or worker, complete population/parameters, schema and source rights; the second real edition when included in the agreement
Original VGI catalog/worker, DuckDB/Arrow application and installed component editions, license terms and actual streaming/direct-file access policy
Selected original merchant and independent buyer deployment IDs; exact acquisition price, aggregate task budget, network, asset, recipient, authority and facilitator selections
The customer's useful SQL/computation task and complete receiving output, including original source population and acquired-edition references
Private receiving host and retained state/configuration references; named source, merchant, catalog/worker, SQL and receiving operators
Agreed refresh trigger, edition/schema change procedure, correction/support allowance and complete independent reopening route
